subject: Proposal: smoothing uplift billing and staged co-term for Glacier Analytics
messages:
From: Mike Chen <mike@glacieranalytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract uplift & billing smoothing options

Hi Priya,

Quick one from our finance and product teams — we scaled usage faster than forecast in May and need to add ~120k tokens/month effective July 1. We want to avoid a single-month billing spike that will trigger internal budget reviews.

Can Redwood offer any of the following: a) staged uplift (spread incremental cost over 2–3 months), b) a temporary discount on the uplifted portion while we confirm steady-state, or c) a co-term path so we can align renewal to the end of Q4 instead of keeping a separate mid-cycle amendment.

We’re open to a short call — Sarah (cc’d) handles procurement. Appreciate proposals or a quick worksheet so we can model cash impact.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
Glacier Analytics

Attachments: none in this message
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike@glacieranalytics.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sliu@glacieranalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift & billing smoothing options

Hi Mike — thanks for the clear ask. We can do each of those options; tradeoffs below and I attached a worksheet so you can see the pro-forma.

Short proposals (high level):
- Staged uplift (recommended): spread the incremental token spend over 3 billing cycles. You’d be billed ~33% of the uplifted run-rate in July, then scale to full effective charge in Sep. This avoids an immediate spike.
- Temporary uplift discount: apply a 10% discount on the incremental tokens for 90 days while usage stabilizes. Discount applies only to tokens above your baseline.
- Co-term: we can create an amendment that annualizes the uplift and co-terms you to 2027-12-31. In that path we can offer a one-time credit equal to the pro-rated difference between the staged path and the annualized rate.

Key questions to settle: baseline token definition, whether you want staged vs. discount, and whether the co-term should be optional at renewal or mandatory now.

I attached "GLA_uplift_workbook_Q3.xlsx" with a few scenarios. If you prefer, we can run numbers with Ben and Sean on this call tomorrow.

Proposed next step: 30-min call at 11:00am PT tomorrow to pick a path.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift & billing smoothing options

Looping in some quick math and an alternate pricing structure we’ve used for other scale-ups — keeping it simple so procurement has a clean line of sight.

Option A — 3-month smoothing (recommended operationally):
- Month 1: bill baseline + 40% of uplifted tokens at listed rate
- Month 2: baseline + 70% of uplifted tokens
- Month 3+: full uplifted run-rate
- No change to overall contract value; cashflow is smoothed.

Option B — 90-day trial discount:
- 10% discount on incremental tokens for first 90 days after effective date
- After 90 days, revert to standard pricing unless you elect co-term annualization, which locks a 5% discount for the remainder of the year.

Option C — Co-term + committed banding:
- Annualize uplift to co-term end (2027-12-31) and offer tiered discount based on uplift band: 0–50k tokens (0%), 50–150k (5%), 150k+ (10%) on incremental band.

I attached a simple grid (staged-co-term-pricing-grid.pdf) with sample dollar flows. Operational notes: staged smoothing requires a single amendment and a one-line billing schedule; co-term needs an updated order form and a credit memo for any retroactive alignment.

If Mike/Sarah want a cleaner cash-impact line to show finance, we can produce two P&L rows (cash vs. GAAP) and a short explanation for their controller.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: staged-co-term-pricing-grid.pdf
From: Mike Chen <mike@glacieranalytics.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift & billing smoothing options

Thanks Priya and Ben — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 
- Finance prefers smoothing over discounts so our CFO doesn’t have to reclassify a spike.
- If we do staged smoothing, can the effective start be 2027-07-01 and the smoothing be backfilled (i.e., the lower staged billing applies retroactively to the start of the month)? We want invoices to reflect the staged amounts rather than summer spikes.
- For the co-term option, procurement asks whether the co-term credit can be applied as a line-item credit on the first co-term invoice vs. a separate credit memo. That simplifies our AR process.

Also, a compliance note: we need the amendment to preserve existing SOC 2 data handling appendices and not change retention terms. Will that be automatic for the amendment?

Let me know and we’ll confirm the 11am PT call if helpful.

—Mike
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike@glacieranalytics.com>, Sarah Liu <sliu@glacieranalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift & billing smoothing options

Mike — great questions. Confirming the following so we can lock language in the amendment: 

1) Start date and backfill: we can make the effective date 2027-07-01 and apply staged billing retroactively for July (i.e., the July invoice will show the staged calculation rather than the raw run-rate). That requires a single amendment and a one-time invoice adjustment; we’ll mark it as a line-item adjustment on the July invoice.

2) Credits & co-term handling: we can apply the co-term credit as a line-item credit on the first invoice after co-term is executed (instead of separate credit memo). That keeps AR clean.

3) Compliance: the amendment will not modify your SOC 2 or data retention appendices — those stay in force. I’ll include the standard clause line: "All technical and organizational controls in the Master Services Agreement remain unchanged by this amendment."

Proposed commercial path (our recommended): staged smoothing over 3 months + optional co-term at renewal with a 5% band discount if you annualize now. I’ve updated the workbook with the retroactive-staging numbers and attached both files. If that works, I’ll get legal to draft the one-page amendment language (amendment + one-line billing schedule) and circulate for signature (DocuSign link below).
